advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether doctor.scan_dirty should also scope untracked_events to active tickets (consistent with fsck's new default) or document the intended asymmetry.
evidence: doctor.scan_dirty has no include_archived filtering (search_files for 'include_archived' in doctor.py returned no matches)
src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:422-429: _dirty_tracker_lines filters classes['untracked_events'] by _dir_is_archived when not include_archived
commit message states 'Like the per-ticket checks, the row covers only active tickets unless --include-archived is given' — this applies only to fsck, not doctor
advisory.finding: doctor's scan_dirty reports the new untracked_events class for ALL tickets including archived ones, while fsck now scopes TRACKER_DIRTY_UNTRACKED_EVENT to active tickets unless --include-archived is given. The two consumers of the shared classifier therefore diverge on scope for this class.
scenarios: An operator runs `doctor` on a store with an untracked event file inside an archived ticket: doctor lists it as a manual finding, but `fsck` (without --include-archived) does not report it, so the two tools disagree about whether the file exists as an issue.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test seeding an untracked event inside an archived ticket and assert it is absent from the row by default and present with --include-archived.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:422-429 adds the archived filter — the progress comment records this was a real regression (archived untracked file wrongly listed) fixed late
tests/unit/test_fsck_untracked_event.py contains three tests, none exercising an ARCHIVED ticket with an untracked event under the default vs --include-archived flag
ABSENCE: no test seeds an archived ticket directory to assert the row is suppressed by default and restored under --include-archived
advisory.finding: The new TRACKER_DIRTY_UNTRACKED_EVENT row's active-only default scope and the snapshot-check reclassification (untracked pre-compaction events no longer surface as snapshot_inconsistent/orphan_event) is a behavior change to the stable `rebar store fsck --output json` surface with no regression test asserting the --include-archived boundary.
scenarios: A future refactor of _dir_is_archived or the scoping filter silently re-breaks the archived-exclusion the progress note calls out as a regression, and no unit test catches it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test seeding an untracked event file in an archived ticket dir and assert it is omitted by default but present under --include-archived.
evidence: search_files for 'include_archived' in tests/unit returned no hits in test_fsck_untracked_event.py or test_doctor_dirty_tree.py

Named violating input: an untracked event file at `<archived-ticket>/<ts>-<uuid>-CREATE.json` where the ticket dir is archived — the default run must omit it and `--include-archived` must include it; neither path is exercised.
advisory.finding: The new include_archived scoping for the TRACKER_DIRTY_UNTRACKED_EVENT row is untested: _dirty_tracker_lines filters out untracked events under archived ticket directories unless include_archived=True, but no test seeds an untracked event inside an archived ticket dir to verify it is hidden by default and surfaced with --include-archived.
scenarios: An archived ticket with a stray untracked event file is wrongly reported (or wrongly omitted) and no test catches the regression.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a doctor --repair test seeding an untracked event file and assert its finding has repair_status=='manual' and the file bytes are unchanged.
evidence: test_doctor_dirty_tree.py:300 only asserts `by_kind["tracker-dirty-tmp-event"]["repair_status"] == "manual"` — no assertion for tracker-dirty-untracked-event
search_files 'untracked' in test_doctor_dirty_tree.py shows only classifier fence/clean-store assertions, no doctor --repair exercise of the new class
advisory.finding: doctor's manual classification of the new untracked-event kind is untested at the doctor level: _MANUAL_DIRTY_KINDS now includes _KIND_DIRTY_UNTRACKED_EVENT and doctor must mark it 'manual' and never move the file, but no doctor test seeds an untracked event file and asserts repair_status=='manual' with the bytes left untouched.
scenarios: doctor --repair on a store with an untracked event file either moves it or mislabels its repair_status; the new manual-class membership could be dropped without any failing test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the exact _retired_copy_note count (e.g. '1 of 1' when a .retired sibling exists, '0 of 1' when it does not) rather than only a 'retired' substring.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:444-445 ADDED: `preserved = sum(... _exists_in_ref(tracker, "HEAD", rel + RETIRED_SUFFIX))` then `f"{preserved} of {len(paths)} have a tracked .retired copy at HEAD"`
test_fsck_untracked_event.py:81 only asserts `assert "retired" in rows[0]["detail"]` — the word 'retired' appears in the literal regardless of the computed count
Named violating input: an untracked event file with NO committed `.retired` sibling should yield '0 of 1' — this branch is never exercised, and no test asserts the '1 of 1' value either
advisory.finding: The _retired_copy_note detail (counting how many untracked events have a committed .retired copy at HEAD) is asserted only via the weak substring `"retired" in rows[0]["detail"]`, which passes for both the '0 of N' and 'N of N' outputs; the zero-preserved branch and the actual count value are untested.
scenarios: A bug that always reports the wrong preserved count (e.g. off-by-one or querying the wrong ref) still passes because the assertion only checks for the static word 'retired'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `rows[0]["detail"].endswith("1 of 1 have a tracked .retired copy at HEAD")` in the preserved case and add a case with no .retired sibling asserting '0 of 1'.
